name: Health Professions Advising Fall Kickoff
description:
The Health Professions Advising Fall Kickoff is an annual advising and community-building event for students interested in or exploring health professions. The event will provide students with an opportunity to complete an HPA Progress Check-In, reflect on their academic and experiential preparation, identify next steps, and learn about advising, programs, events, and application resources available through Health Professions Advising during the 2026–2027 academic year.

Students will also have opportunities to connect with HPA peer guides and other students pursuing or considering health professions, with the goal of strengthening peer support and helping students learn from one another across class years and career interests. The event is open to students from all years and concentrations, including students who are still exploring whether a health profession may be a good fit.

Boba will be provided to students who register in advance and complete the HPA Declare Pre-Health form, which allows Health Professions Advising to identify and better support students interested in health professions throughout the academic year.

name: Moving Mountains: Asian American and Pacific Islander Feminisms and the 1977 National Women's Conference
description: Judy Tzu-Chun Wu is a professor of History and Asian American Studies at the University of California, Irvine. She also is associate dean of research, faculty development, and public engagement in the School of Humanities, the director of the Humanities Center, and the director of the Center for Liberation, Anti-Racism, and Belonging (C-LAB). She specializes in Asian American, immigration, comparative racialization, women's, gender, and sexuality histories. Wu received her Ph.D. in U.S. History from Stanford University and previously taught at Ohio State University. Wu's most recent book is Moving Mountains: Asian American and Pacific Islander Feminisms and the 1977 National Women's Conference (2026). Her talk will focus on her research and her new book and will further the REHR Center’s mission by connecting rigorous scholarship with broader conversations about race, ethnicity, justice, and human rights.

name: Fitness Classes: Tabata
description:
Class Description: Tabata is a style of cardio conditioning with 20 seconds of maximum effort, followed by 10 seconds of rest for 4 minutes. We will start with a warm-up, do several intervals and end with a cool down. Good for endurance!

name: Fitness Classes: Yoga
description:
Class Description: Embodied Flow This one-hour yoga experience blends Vinyasa flow and Pilates-inspired movement to cultivate strength, balance, and release. Each class begins with a moment of intention-setting, inviting you to ground your energy and arrive fully in the body. By integrating breath, presence, and intentional movement, students are guided to move with awareness and acceptance. Sessions emphasize core strength, stability, and increased range of motion. Students of all levels are welcome.

Truth is found in the breath.

Fitness Classes are open to all students, staff and faculty! There is no need to sign up for the class, just arrive 5 minutes before the start of class and bring some water! name: Soka Health Research Symposium: Conference-Bound Scholarship in Public Health, Global Health, Epidemiology, Bioethics, and Health Policy
description:
Join us for an evening celebrating research that Soka students, recent alumni, and faculty will present at the Sexual Violence Research Initiative (SVRI) Forum, American Society for Bioethics and Humanities (ASBH) Annual Meeting, Gerontological Society of America (GSA) Annual Scientific Meeting, and American Public Health Association (APHA) Annual Meeting this fall. Presenters will share scholarship in public health, global health, epidemiology, bioethics, health policy, environmental health, aging, maternal and child health, mental health, and related disciplines. Preview research before it reaches national and international conferences, meet the researchers, and explore opportunities to pursue health-related scholarship.

Following the oral presentations, attendees can visit posters and roundtable presentations, meet the researchers, and ask questions in an informal setting.

We also welcome presentations by students, recent alumni, and faculty who will present research in public health, global health, bioethics, or related health disciplines at a professional conference this year. If you are interested in participating, please contact the organizers.

The event will also highlight the final application deadline for the Soka Health Advocacy and Research Program (SHARP) Internship, sponsored by Health Professions Advising (HPA) and the Career Development Office (CDO).

Join us afterward for refreshments and conversation with the presenters.

name: Johns Hopkins University & University of Pennsylvania Schools of Nursing Information Session
description:
Co-sponsored by Health Professions Advising and the Career Development Office

Join admissions representatives from the Johns Hopkins University School of Nursing and the University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing for an in-person information session exploring pathways into the nursing profession through accelerated entry programs.

Representatives will provide an overview of their nationally recognized nursing programs, including accelerated Master of Nursing and other graduate entry pathways for students who have completed a bachelor's degree in another discipline. The session will also discuss admissions requirements, prerequisite coursework, clinical training, financial aid, career opportunities, and what distinguishes each institution's approach to nursing education.

Students considering careers in nursing, advanced practice nursing, public health, or healthcare leadership are encouraged to attend. This is an excellent opportunity to learn about the profession, ask questions directly of admissions officers, and gain insights into preparing a competitive application.

Guest Speaker: Chris Jermyn, Associate Director of Admissions, University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing
Laura Panozzo, Associate Director Admissions, Johns Hopkins University School of Nursing

name: Humanism & Health Speaker Series
description:
The inaugural session of the Humanism & Health Speaker Series will take place virtually on October 16, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. PT and will feature Victoria A. Smith, MD, Associate Medical Director for Primary Care at Ochsner Health, in conversation with Soka University of America Student Fellow Kiarra Hoes.

Co-hosted by Soka University of America and the WHO Collaborating Centre for Healthy Cities and Urban Policy Research at the Institute of Science Tokyo, the Humanism & Health Speaker Series examines how health professionals and leaders translate humanistic values into practice across clinical care, health systems, public and global health, and planetary health. Through an interview-based conversation, Dr. Smith will discuss how humanism informs her approach to patient care and health care leadership.

name: 2026 Summer Clinical Grand Rounds & Clinical Preceptorship Info Session
description: This Summer Clinical Preceptorship Grand Rounds will feature case discussions presented by students who completed preceptorship program in 2026. Isabel Pizano-Canales, Taiho Higaki, and Calleigh Sakai will present clinical cases from both the Primary Care / Population Health Track and the Neurosurgery Track, outlining the diagnostic reasoning, management approaches, and clinical observations they encountered during their training. Following the case presentations, we will provide information about the upcoming Summer Clinical Preceptorship, including program expectations and application details. This session is open to the campus community. We strongly encourage those considering applying for the next preceptorship cycle to attend.

description: Conversations in Research Panel Discussion Series. This session will focus on the crucial first step in research: turning a broad interest or curiosity into a viable, sharp research question. Faculty panelists will share strategies and experiences in narrowing scope, identifying research gaps, and knowing when a question is ready to guide a full project. Join us for this enlightening presentation to learn how to best prepare your research topic.

name: Become a Physician: Exploring the DO Pathway with AACOM

The session will provide an overview of osteopathic medicine and the pathway to becoming a Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO), including osteopathic medical education, the AACOMAS application process, admissions expectations, application timelines, and factors to consider when exploring DO medical schools. Participants will also have an opportunity to ask questions.

description:
Join the Orange County School of the Arts Classical Voice Conservatory
Choirs and the Instrumental Music Conservatory Symphony Orchestra in a
celebration of 40 years of music at the Orange County School of the
Arts.  Featuring an 80-piece orchestra and 103 singers, this concert
will spotlight the incredible talent and artistry in a kaleidoscope of
musical masterworks, including Serenade to Music by Ralph Vaughan
Williams.
